description: Pure DATA + map definitions. A finite LIBRARY of local CPTP maps (quantum channels) acting on a single-qubit density operator rho (2x2 PSD, trace 1). The object computed is the NONCOMMUTATION MATRIX delta(A,B,rho) = || A(B(rho)) - B(A(rho)) ||_1 (trace norm) over ALL ordered pairs (A,B) of maps in the library, evaluated on a fixed probe state rho0 and a small bank of probe states. The N01 witness: ORDER MATTERS for the pair (A,B) iff delta(A,B,rho) > 0. No deltas are precomputed or asserted here; each engine derives the full matrix from the actual channel action (Kraus / superoperator), not from a label.
carrier: single qubit. rho = 2x2 complex Hermitian PSD matrix, trace 1. Probe bank: rho0 = |+><+| (the X-eigenstate, off-diagonal, generic under all six maps); plus a maximally-mixed state I/2, a |0><0| pole, and a generic Bloch-interior state. The full ordered-pair matrix is reported on EVERY probe; the headline matrix is on rho0.

Ti_z_dephasing.role: z-axis dephasing channel (decoheres the X/Y coherences, leaves Z populations)
Ti_z_dephasing.kraus: K0 = sqrt(1-p/2) I, K1 = sqrt(p/2) Z, with p=1 (full dephasing). Equivalent: rho -> diag(rho) (kills off-diagonals).
Ti_z_dephasing.cptp: trace-preserving + completely positive (Choi PSD) -- checked, not asserted

Te_x_dephasing.role: x-axis dephasing channel (decoheres in the X basis)
Te_x_dephasing.kraus: H Z H conjugation of Ti: dephase in the Hadamard (X) basis. K0 = sqrt(1-p/2) I, K1 = sqrt(p/2) X-basis-Z, p=1.

Fi_x_rotation.role: unitary x-rotation Rx(theta) = exp(-i theta X /2), theta = pi/3 (a generic angle, NOT pi/2 which can collapse a gap)

Fe_z_rotation.role: unitary z-rotation Rz(phi) = exp(-i phi Z /2), phi = pi/4 (generic angle)

projector_pinch.role: measure-and-forget pinch onto the Z basis: rho -> P0 rho P0 + P1 rho P1 (a projective non-unitary CPTP map; this is exactly the Z-dephasing pinch and so is INTENTIONALLY equal in action to Ti -- a built-in commuting/identity-of-action pair used as a discriminator)

Lindblad_amp_damp.role: amplitude-damping dissipator (energy relaxation toward |0>) at damping gamma = 0.3

noncommutation_matrix.definition: delta[A][B](rho) = trace_norm( A(B(rho)) - B(A(rho)) ), trace_norm(M) = sum of singular values of M = sum |eigenvalues| for Hermitian M.
noncommutation_matrix.diagonal: delta[A][A] = 0 identically (a map commutes with itself); reported for completeness, EXCLUDED from the noncommutation evidence because it is by-construction zero.
noncommutation_matrix.symmetry: delta[A][B] == delta[B][A] by definition (the commutator A B - B A is antisymmetric in (A,B); its trace norm equals that of B A - A B). The matrix is SYMMETRIC; this is a structural check, not a discovered fact.
noncommutation_matrix.scan: all ordered pairs (A,B), A != B, over the 6 maps -> 30 off-diagonal entries (15 unordered).

genuine_discriminators.a_commuting_pair_zero: STRUCTURAL (by-construction) commuting pairs, recorded but NOT discovered: Ti_z_dephasing == projector_pinch (identical channel action by design); Fe_z_rotation vs Ti_z_dephasing and Fe_z_rotation vs projector_pinch (Rz is diagonal in the Z eigenbasis, commutes with any Z-diagonal map for ALL rho). These commute as SUPEROPERATORS (max delta over the d^2 probe basis ~ 0), confirmable by algebra without simulation. See by_construction_index and map_level_commutation. They are confirmations of known algebra, not noncommutation discoveries.
genuine_discriminators.b_genuinely_noncommuting_pair_positive: On rho0 = |+><+| the COMPUTED genuinely-noncommuting pairs are {Fe_z_rotation - Te_x_dephasing (delta=0.7071), Fe_z_rotation - Fi_x_rotation (delta=0.7071), Lindblad_amp_damp - Fi_x_rotation (delta=0.3000)} -- all derived from the Kraus action, with deltas that VARY continuously with the rotation/damping parameters. NOTE: Lindblad_amp_damp - Te_x_dephasing was REMOVED from the genuine set: delta(La,Te,rho) = GAMMA for EVERY rho (commutator difference = diag(GAMMA/2,-GAMMA/2), probe-independent; the value equals the damping parameter). It is a by-construction NONZERO recorded under by_construction_index, not a probe-discovered order effect.
genuine_discriminators.b2_probe_relative_order_dependence: The pair Ti_z_dephasing - Fi_x_rotation (z-dephasing vs x-rotation) is PROBE-RELATIVE: delta = 0 on rho0 = |+><+| and on I/2 but delta > 0 on the |0><0| pole (0.8660) and on a generic Bloch-interior state (0.3122). The zeros on |+> and I/2 are BY-CONSTRUCTION fixed-point zeros (Ti(|+>)=I/2 is a fixed point of all unitaries; I/2 is a fixed point of both maps) -- they are state-null kernels of the commutator superoperator, NOT map-level commutation. The genuine probe-relativity evidence is the NONZERO on pole0 and generic: Ti-Fi is a NONCOMMUTING superoperator (max delta over the d^2 basis = 0.866) that merely vanishes on the |+> probe. CORRECTION: a by-construction sim CAN produce a single-probe zero that 'flips' to nonzero on another probe -- it just means rho0 lies in the commutator kernel. Map-level commutation must be classified by the MAX delta over a tomographically complete (d^2=4) probe basis, not by a single probe.
genuine_discriminators.c_antisymmetric_structure: the commutator superoperator [L_A, L_B] is antisymmetric in (A,B); delta is its symmetric trace-norm magnitude. The signed structure (which order yields more Y-coherence) is checked via Tr(Y (A(B(rho)) - B(A(rho)))), which flips sign under the (a,b) swap -- a signed antisymmetry check, not just the magnitude.
genuine_discriminators.d_classical_diagonal_baseline_collapses: restrict the probe state to a CLASSICAL (diagonal in Z) rho and the map library to the Z-basis-preserving subset {Ti, projector_pinch, Lindblad, Fe}: on diagonal states Ti/projector_pinch/Lindblad map diagonal->diagonal and Fe_z_rotation (Rz, a unitary) acts as the IDENTITY on diagonal states (phases cancel on populations -- it is NOT a stochastic map, correction to earlier wording). All four therefore commute on diagonal states -> the noncommutation GAP collapses (delta ~ 0 across the classical sub-block). CAVEAT (deepseek/glm finding): this collapse is structurally FORCED by the choice of Z-preserving maps, not a discovered classical fact; the negative control 'COULD fail' only for a genuinely classical-noncommuting pair, which this sub-block does not contain. The NONTRIVIAL part is the RE-OPEN: adding a coherence-carrying map (Fi x-rotation) on the SAME classical state gives delta>0 (0.346), because Rx creates off-diagonal coherence from a diagonal state that the two orderings then process differently -- showing the gap is carried by coherence.

controls.commuting_control: Ti_z_dephasing vs projector_pinch -> delta = 0 (their channel actions coincide). COULD fail if the actions differed.
controls.identity_map_control: add an identity channel id(rho)=rho to the library; delta[id][X] = 0 for every X (identity commutes with everything). COULD fail if id were mis-implemented.
controls.label_shuffle_invariant: permute the map NAMES (relabel) and recompute: the delta matrix is invariant under relabeling up to the row/column permutation (the physics does not depend on the nickname). A label-shuffle that CHANGED a delta value would expose a name-dependence bug.
controls.classical_diagonal_baseline: on classical diagonal rho with the diagonal-map sub-block, all pairwise deltas are 0 -> the gap is carried by coherence, not by the label. COULD fail (and would, for any genuinely classical-noncommuting pair, but stochastic maps on populations commute).

cptp_validity.trace_preserving: sum_k K_k^dag K_k == I checked per map to 1e-12. This is the LOAD-BEARING CPTP gate: it DOES reject a non-TP map (verified: K=[I,I] gives sum=2I, TP error 1.0).
cptp_validity.complete_positivity: Choi matrix C = sum_k vec(K_k) vec(K_k)^dag is recorded with its min eigenvalue, BUT this PSD check is a TAUTOLOGY for any Kraus list: a sum of rank-1 PSD outer products is always PSD (verified: 2000 random 2-Kraus sets all give min eig >= -8e-15). The Choi-PSD pass therefore CANNOT reject a non-CP map given a Kraus representation and is NOT counted as evidence of complete positivity. The Choi object is built with the standard row-major (Choi-Jamiolkowski) vec convention in all four engines (julia previously used a column-major vec that produced a different Choi object with a coincidentally-correct verdict; fixed).
cptp_validity.convention_note: All four legs use K.reshape(-1,1) row-major vec; julia uses reshape(permutedims(K),4,1) to match.

invariant_to_agree_on.delta_matrix_rho0: the full 6x6 off-diagonal trace-norm matrix on rho0 = |+><+|, agreed across 4 engines to 1e-9
invariant_to_agree_on.map_level_commutation: the MAP-LEVEL (superoperator) commuting set, classified by max delta over a tomographically complete (d^2=4) probe basis, agreed across engines. This separates true superoperator commutation (9 pairs) from state-null zeros on rho0 (2 pairs: Ti-Fi, Fi-projector_pinch, which are noncommuting maps that vanish on |+>).
invariant_to_agree_on.commuting_pairs_rho0: the set of (A,B) with delta == 0 on rho0 (within 1e-9) -- a SINGLE-PROBE classification (11 pairs), reported but superseded by map_level_commutation for any commutation claim.
invariant_to_agree_on.noncommuting_pairs: the set of (A,B) with delta > 1e-9, agreed across engines
invariant_to_agree_on.controls: commuting_control == 0, identity_control == 0 for all, classical_diagonal gap == 0, label_shuffle invariant -- all agreed (these are by-construction structural checks, recorded not load-bearing)

engines.numpy_exact: dense 2x2 complex matrices, Kraus sums, scipy/numpy eigenvalues for the trace norm. Reference substrate.
engines.jax: jnp complex128 dense Kraus action + jnp.linalg.svdvals for the trace norm; x64 enabled. Distinct array library / distinct trace-norm path (singular values).
engines.pytorch: torch complex128 Kraus action + torch.linalg.eigvalsh on the Hermitian difference for the trace norm (sum of |eigvals|). Distinct framework + distinct trace-norm route (Hermitian eig, not SVD).
engines.julia: from-scratch reimplementation: native ComplexF64 matrices, Kraus sums, LinearAlgebra.svdvals for the trace norm. Independent language; reads no peer result.

earns: a NARROW diagnostic fact: on a 6-map single-qubit CPTP library, the noncommutation matrix delta(A,B,rho)=||[A,B](rho)||_1 is COMPUTED (not asserted). MAP-LEVEL commutation, classified by max delta over a tomographically complete (d^2=4) probe basis, separates (i) 9 genuinely superoperator-commuting pairs -- all confirmations of known algebra (Z-diagonal maps commute; identical-action maps; Rx commutes with x-dephasing; scalar phase commutes with scalar damping), (ii) genuinely noncommuting pairs with parameter-VARYING deltas (Fe vs x-axis maps = sin(phi); Lindblad vs Fi), and (iii) 2 STATE-NULL zeros that are noncommuting maps vanishing only on the |+> probe (Ti-Fi, Fi-projector_pinch). Ti-Fi is genuinely PROBE-RELATIVE: it is a noncommuting superoperator (max basis delta 0.866) whose value is 0 on |+> and I/2 but 0.866 on |0> and 0.312 on a generic state. The classical-diagonal gap collapse is structurally forced (Z-preserving subset); the RE-OPEN under a coherence map (Fi) is the nontrivial part. Four independent engines (3 distinct trace-norm routes, 4 languages/frameworks) agree to 2.8e-16. This witnesses N01 (order-matters-iff-delta>0) at the channel level, with probe-relativity, WITHOUT smuggling the answer in. By-construction items (Choi-PSD tautology, Lindblad-vs-Te = GAMMA, structural zeros, fixed-point zeros) are explicitly labeled in by_construction_index and excluded from the genuine evidence.
does_not_earn: any claim that this is the canonical operator-precedence / Axis-6 layer; any chirality, bridge, GNVW, manifold-forcing, or emergence claim; any multi-qubit precedence result (this is single-qubit + a 2-qubit note only if computed); promotion past scratch_diagnostic. The map library is a CHOSEN convenience set, not a forced basis.

lineage.root_axiom: a = a iff a ~ b -- identity is probe-relative. Here the probe family is the CPTP map library; two orderings are indistinguishable (a~b) iff delta = 0 under the trace-norm probe.
lineage.n01_root: N01 = noncommutation root: order is load-bearing iff applying A then B differs from B then A under an active distinguishing probe (trace norm).
lineage.exclusion_first: delta = 0 EXCLUDES order-dependence for that pair (the two orderings are indistinguishable); delta > 0 admits it. The matrix records which orderings are excluded vs admitted, it does not 'generate' an order.
